blocks.text:
After breakfast, you will take a sightseeing tour of Quito and travel to the equator.

Quito lies at an altitude of about 2,800 m. Founded in the 16th century on the ruins of an Inca settlement, its historic centre has retained its colonial buildings, churches, domes, courtyards and richly decorated interiors despite the earthquake of 1917. The Quito School of Art developed here, bringing together Spanish, Italian, Moorish, Flemish and Indigenous traditions.

During a one-and-a-half-hour walk through the Old Town, you will see why Quito was among the first places to become a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The city's name is associated with the Quitus people, who lived in the region long before the Spanish conquest. In 1533, the city came under the control of Sebastián de Benalcázar, and in 1541 it received Spanish city status and its full name, San Francisco de Quito.

Artists of the Quito School worked in stone and wood, creating religious sculptures and decorative elements for churches. The tour therefore goes beyond facades and squares: much of the experience lies in the interiors, carving and the way European artistic traditions intertwined with local ones.

The Franciscans were the first religious order to establish itself in the city. Their monastery became a centre of education, painting and sculpture. Plaza Grande is home to the Cathedral, Presidential Palace, Archbishop's Palace and City Hall. The programme also includes the Jesuit church, known for its intricate carving and richly decorated interior.

A separate stop is planned at the Basilica del Voto Nacional. It was designed by a French architect inspired by Notre-Dame de Paris. Construction began in the 19th century. The facade features animals of Ecuador and the region, including caimans, tortoises, boobies and monkeys. The building is 140 m long and 35 m wide, with a central nave 30 m high. Its two front towers rise to 115 m.

You will then go up El Panecillo. The viewpoint offers a panorama of Quito's old and new districts, beneath a winged statue of the Virgin Mary.

After the city tour, the route continues to the Middle of the World, with two visits.

**Mitad del Mundo.** This visitor complex commemorates the geodetic expedition of 1736, which determined the position of the equator. A 30-metre monument was erected here in 1979–1982, with a line marking the equator. GPS measurements later showed that the actual equator lies about 240 m further north.

**Intiñán Museum.** Demonstrations associated with the equator include swirling water, balancing an egg and walking along the equator line. The exhibits also introduce the cultures of the region's ancient peoples, the tsantsa ritual, totems and traditional dwellings. Among the exhibits is a house containing possessions of a family that lived in the area for many generations. This part of the day offers a change from a conventional city tour: Quito's colonial architecture gives way to geography, ethnography and the history of Ecuador's peoples.

After the tour, return to the hotel for a free evening.

**Stops:** Basilica of the National Vow, Main Square, Golden Church, San Francisco Square, El Panecillo, Intiñán Museum, Middle of the World.  
**Accommodation:** Ikala 3*.  
**Meals:** breakfast.
